translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every choice of types P, D, E and R, every record t of type S3 P D E R, and every r in R, let A be the set of p in P for which some o in t.c1(p) satisfies t.c3(o) = r. For each p in P, let B(p) be the set of e in E that belong to t.c2(o) for some o in t.c1(p), whether or not t.c3(o) = r. If there exists a function S from A to A and there exists a p in A such that B(p) and B(S(p)) are disjoint, then there exists an o in D such that t.c3(o) = r, o belongs to t.c1(q) for some q in P, and t.c4(t.c3(o)) does not belong to t.c2(o). Disjointness is required only for the witnessing p, not for every member of A; S(p) need not differ from p. The conclusion does not require q to be p or S(p).

judgement.summary: D21 matches Definition 3.1: the transformation preserves the class of configurations capable of producing inference content r, and disjoint predictions are required for at least one configuration. The conclusion gives a falsification at a producible dataset with content r, as in Lemma 3.5; dropping the content condition gives Lemma 3.3.
